cl_mdma_empathy.q: Does MDMA really make you more empathic, or just feel like it?
cl_mdma_empathy.short: Partly: people feel warmer, but they don't read others better. In a lab test, they named 55 in 100 fearful faces correctly on MDMA, against 63 on a dummy pill.
cl_mdma_empathy.but: These were small lab studies. People rated photos and played a money game instead of talking with real people.
how: 21 people who had used ecstasy took MDMA, meth or a dummy pill on different days. MDMA raised 'loving' and 'friendly' ratings over the dummy pill, but not clearly over meth. Only meth clearly raised 'sociable'.

In the same study, faces flashed up for half a second. People named 55 in 100 fearful faces right on MDMA, against 63 on the dummy pill. An earlier study of 9 people, with clear faces shown for 4 seconds, found no change.

In Basel, 32 healthy people felt a bit more for people in photos on MDMA (about 5.0 against 4.4 out of 9), but got worse at naming fear, anger, disgust and surprise. Oxytocin rose, but didn't match these changes.
In a money game with real payouts, people more often picked the split that gave the other person the most. Most volunteers could tell they'd had MDMA, and many tests were run.
cl_mdma_empathy.rate: Two small lab studies from different teams, each comparing MDMA with a dummy pill in the same people. Both found fear harder to spot; the feelings are people's own ratings, and the money game was tried in one study.

cl_mdma_sex.q: What does MDMA do to sex drive, erections and orgasm?
cl_mdma_sex.short: Desire often goes up, erections can go either way, and orgasm often takes longer. In one survey, 8 of 20 men said erections got weaker on MDMA, and 8 stronger.
cl_mdma_sex.but: It's 35 people who chose to talk about it, remembering past experiences. Nobody tested their pills.
how: In Israel, 20 men and 15 women who had used MDMA before sex compared it, from memory, with their usual sex. All 35 said desire went up, and 32 said they were more satisfied.
Of the 20 men, 8 said erections got weaker and 8 stronger. Orgasm took longer for 16 of 20 men and 6 of 15 women, and 3 people couldn't reach it, yet still felt more satisfied.
In Northern Ireland, 98 people were interviewed. A little over half said MDMA was more about closeness than sex. Some men couldn't get an erection; others described strong desire.
Some described one-night stands and regret. Condoms were rare on ecstasy, but also rare without drugs, so the study can't show MDMA made sex riskier.
cl_mdma_sex.rate: Two small studies from the 1990s: a survey of 35 people who chose to take part and remembered the past, and interviews without counts. Nobody tested the pills or compared times with and without MDMA.

cl_mdma_hyponatremia.q: Can drinking lots of water on MDMA lead to low blood salt?
cl_mdma_hyponatremia.short: Possibly. Low blood salt (sodium) after MDMA has been reported, mostly in young people; of 17 UK cases, at least 10 had drunk a lot of liquid.
cl_mdma_hyponatremia.but: These only count people who got ill. So they can't show how often it happens, or whether drinking more changes the risk.
how: Over 28 months, 17 people aged 15 to 26 were reported to a UK poisons service. Of the 15 who survived, 10 had seizures, 12 had a normal temperature at hospital, and 13 recovered fully.
The 2 who died, aged 15 and 18, had brain swelling. Both had drunk a lot of water, and drank or were given more after they began to feel ill.
In California poison-centre records, 73 of 188 people who had their blood salt measured had a low level. 4 of those 73 died.

The papers think MDMA makes the body hold on to water. In one study, 8 healthy men given one MDMA capsule had a rise in the water-holding hormone, and their blood salt fell a little, not to a low level. It had no proper comparison, and a study of 32 people found no clear rise in a related marker.
cl_mdma_hyponatremia.rate: Records from two poison services, in the UK and California, which agree. But MDMA was confirmed by tests in only some cases, and in California only about a third had blood salt measured.

general.statement: MDMA helps you tell what other people feel.
general.why: In lab tests, people felt warmer on MDMA but didn't read others better, and they named fear correctly less often. These were small studies using photos.

mdma.statement: On MDMA, people felt more for others in photos but got worse at spotting fear.
mdma.why: In one study, people felt a bit more for people in photos on MDMA but named fear, anger, disgust and surprise correctly less often. Another study also found fear harder to spot.

mdma.statement: Most men get harder erections on MDMA.
mdma.why: In one survey of 20 men, 8 said erections got weaker on MDMA and 8 said stronger. They were remembering past experiences, and nobody tested their pills.

mdma.statement: In one survey, most men who had used MDMA before sex said orgasm took longer.
mdma.why: 16 of 20 men said so, and 6 of 15 women, yet 32 of 35 people said they were more satisfied. It's one small survey of people remembering the past.

mdma.statement: In UK reports, most people with low blood salt after MDMA had drunk a lot of liquid.
mdma.why: At least 10 of 17 cases reported to a UK poisons service had, and the 2 who died had brain swelling. These reports count only people who got ill, so they can't show how often it happens or whether drinking more changes the risk.
